content: Flask-SQLAlchemy's scoped_session is keyed by thread/greenlet identity, not by individual app-context object, and session.remove() fires on teardown_appcontext when the app context is popped. A single thread that pushes one app_context() and keeps it open for its entire lifetime (fine for a short-lived, single-task thread that then exits) is a different case from a long-lived thread that loops forever: holding one context open across many ticks risks stale identity-map state and does not get the automatic session.remove() cleanup between ticks. The safe pattern for a long-lived loop is to push a fresh 'with app.app_context():' block per tick/iteration (not once outside the loop), so each tick gets an implicit fresh scoped session and automatic cleanup at the end of that tick via teardown_appcontext.
